newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgutneftgaz may increase charter capital.
newsitem.headline: Surgutneftgaz may increase charter capital.

text.p: Russian oil company Surgutneftgaz has approved a new company charter which permits the additional issuance of 269,144 ordinary shares and 260,422 preferred shares with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles.

The new charter allows an increase or decrease in charter capital through the placement of additional shares within a stated total or by increasing the shares' face value. It also permits a decrease in face value or total quantity, including by buying back and annulling a part of the company's shares.

The decision on increasing the charter capital through increasing the nominal value of shares or through additional shares in a set quantity was accepted by the company's board of directors and set out in a document.
The document says the current charter capital of the oil company is 10,058,023,000 roubles ($1.75 million) and is divided into 10,058,023 ordinary shares with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles.
On January 1, 1997, the charter capital of Surgutneftgaz was 9,979 billion roubles.

"The increase was made by 78,654 shares, which were issued to exchange shares of the factory Kirishinefteorgsintez, and also Tvernefteprodukt, Pskovnefteprodukt, Kaliningradnefteprodukt, Novgorognefteprodukt," NK Surgutneftegaz Vice President Natalya Olshanova told journalists. --Aleksandras Budris, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
